output_json.patch_notes: Source fix in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile: after `final File f = FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName);` a guard rejects entries that escape the destination via `if (!isInDirectory(dir, f)) throw new ArchiverException(...)`. The private static isInDirectory(destination, f) compares canonical paths, walking f's parent chain up to the canonical destination; it returns false (reject) on any IOException during canonicalization. The check runs before mkdirs/symlink/file-write, so no partial escape occurs. The regression test (TarUnArchiverPathTraversalTest) crafts a TAR containing "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" via commons-compress (already a project dependency), extracts with the real TarUnArchiver, and asserts an ArchiverException is thrown and the marker never appears outside the destination.
output_json.risk_notes: The fix rejects (throws) on traversing entries rather than silently skipping, matching the POV's expectation and failing fast on malicious archives. Legitimate archives with normal nested paths still extract correctly (full existing test suite passes, including tar/zip/jar/war extraction tests). Canonicalization resolves symlinks; on unusual setups where the destination directory itself is a symlink, entries are still validated against the canonical destination, which is the intended containment. IOException during canonicalization is treated as unsafe (rejected), which is conservative. Verified: POV now exits 1 (was 0), new regression test passes, and `mvn -B test` reports BUILD SUCCESS with no new failures.
output_json.summary: Fixed the CWE-022 path traversal ("Zip Slip") in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile by validating that each archive entry resolves inside the destination directory. Previously FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) was used directly, so an entry named "../pov-escaped-marker.txt" could be written outside the destination. Now a new isInDirectory() helper canonicalizes both the destination and the resolved target and walks the target's parent chain; if the resolved file is not the destination or a descendant, an ArchiverException is thrown before any file/dir/symlink is created. This covers all unarchivers (TAR and ZIP paths) since they all route through extractFile. Added a regression test that builds a malicious TAR with a "../" entry and asserts extraction throws and the escaped file is never created.
